name: Phuket Town
seoTitle: Phuket Town: Area Guide, Rents & Property
seoDescription: Phuket Town: the island's commercial and cultural centre with the Old Town, hospitals, schools and the lowest rents. Area guide, rents, rental market and FAQ.
intro: Phuket Town is the island's capital and commercial centre, known for its colourful Sino-Portuguese Old Town, markets and food. It has the main hospitals, schools and government offices, and generally the lowest rents on the island.
overview:
Phuket Town is on the east side of the island, about 20 to 30 minutes by car from the west-coast beaches. The Old Town around Thalang, Dibuk and Krabi roads has restored shophouses, cafes and galleries, while the newer parts of town have shopping malls, hospitals and housing estates.
Our catalogue lists projects in and around the town as well as in the neighbouring areas of Ko Kaeo and Kathu.
suitableFor: Families who want schools and hospitals nearby
Lovers of local food and culture
highlights: Historic Old Town with Sino-Portuguese shophouses
Main hospitals, schools and government offices
Sunday walking street market on Thalang Road
Lowest average rents on the island

lifestyle: Phuket Town is a real Thai city: fresh markets, street food and restaurants, cafes, the Sunday walking street, Khao Rang viewpoint and Saphan Hin park. Daily life is cheaper than in the beach areas, and hospitals, schools and shopping centres are close by.
beaches: Phuket Town has no swimming beach; the coast here is mangroves and a harbour. The nearest beaches on the west and south coasts are about 20 to 30 minutes away by car.
rentalMarket: Phuket Town is mainly a long-term rental market with the lowest typical rents on the island. Tenants include Thai and foreign professionals, teachers, medical staff, students and families; holiday demand is small.

rentalDetails.title: Long-term rentals
rentalDetails.text: Steady demand for practical condos, townhouses and houses close to work, schools and hospitals.

rentalDetails.title: Short-term rentals
rentalDetails.text: Limited; mostly business travellers and visitors to the Old Town.

rentalDetails.title: Suitable property types
rentalDetails.text: Studios and 1-bedroom condos, townhouses and family houses.

rentalDetails.title: Advantages and limitations
rentalDetails.text: Advantage: affordable rents and year-round local demand. Limitations: no beach and lower rents than tourist areas.

investment: Phuket Town suits buyers looking for affordable property and long-term tenants rather than holiday income. Rents are lower than in the beach areas, but demand from people living and working in town is steady.

investmentDetails.title: Risks to consider
investmentDetails.text: Lower rents than tourist areas; older buildings may need renovation.

investmentDetails.title: Ownership costs
investmentDetails.text: Common fees, maintenance and periods between tenants.

faq.question: Is Phuket Town a good place to live?
faq.answer: Phuket Town suits people who want city life, local food, hospitals and schools nearby and lower living costs than the beach areas.

faq.question: Are there beaches in Phuket Town?
faq.answer: No. The nearest beaches on the west and south coasts are about 20 to 30 minutes away by car.

faq.question: Can foreigners buy property in Phuket Town?
faq.answer: Yes, within Thai rules: condominium units can be owned freehold within a building's 49% foreign quota, while townhouses, houses and land are usually bought on a registered lease or through other legal structures. Check the title with a lawyer.

faq.question: What is the Phuket Old Town?
faq.answer: The historic centre around Thalang, Dibuk and Krabi roads, with colourful Sino-Portuguese shophouses, cafes, galleries and a Sunday walking street market.

faq.question: Which hospitals are in Phuket Town?
faq.answer: Phuket Town has the island's main hospitals, including the government Vachira Phuket Hospital and private hospitals such as Bangkok Hospital Phuket.
